Please note that "yoy" refers to "year-over-year." For U.S. core inflation, the most common measure is the **Core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index**. This is the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge.

Here is the year-over-year Core PCE inflation rate from January 2015 to December 2016:

| Date   | Core PCE (YOY %) |
| :----- | :--------------: |
| Jan-15 | 1.3              |
| Feb-15 | 1.4              |
| Mar-15 | 1.4              |
| Apr-15 | 1.2              |
| May-15 | 1.2              |
| Jun-15 | 1.3              |
| Jul-15 | 1.3              |
| Aug-15 | 1.3              |
| Sep-15 | 1.4              |
| Oct-15 | 1.4              |
| Nov-15 | 1.4              |
| Dec-15 | 1.4              |
| Jan-16 | 1.7              |
| Feb-16 | 1.7              |
| Mar-16 | 1.6              |
| Apr-16 | 1.6              |
| May-16 | 1.6              |
| Jun-16 | 1.6              |
| Jul-16 | 1.6              |
| Aug-16 | 1.7              |
| Sep-16 | 1.7              |
| Oct-16 | 1.7              |
| Nov-16 | 1.7              |
| Dec-16 | 1.8              |

**Source:** U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) - Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE), Price Index, Excluding Food and Energy, Percent Change from Year Ago.
